title: 303rd BG (H) Combat Mission No. 78, 14 October 1943 (mission report compilation, incl. 1st Air Division dispatch table and 303rd assembly formation chart)
author: 303rd Bomb Group (H) Association (compiled from group records)
notes: Association transcription of group records. Contains table 'The First Air Division dispatched 149 B-17s': 40th CW (lead wing, Col. Peaslee) 92BG(19) lead, 306BG(18) high, 305BG(16) low = 53; 1st CW (#2 wing, Col. Milton) 91BG(11) lead, 381BG(17) high, 351BG(16) low = 44; 41st CBW (#3 wing, Col. Rohr) 379BG(17) lead, 303BG(19) high, 384BG(16) low = 52. Table columns are typeset with a one-row offset; read as above. Same document states 303rd 'Crews Dispatched: 20' (assembly chart shows 20 incl. 2 aborts), bombing altitude 24,050 ft, 1 lost + 1 abandoned over England. 3rd AD 142 B-17s; 2nd AD 29 B-24s on diversion.

title: 351st BG Group Mission #49, 14 Oct. 1943, Target: North Bearing Works, Schweinfurt (briefing outline, narratives, bombing flight record, flak report, J-form)
author: 351st Bomb Group Association (transcribed group records)
notes: Most detailed primary text found. Briefing: 'Wing Formation - Lead 91st @ 23,000', High 351st @ 24,000, Low 381st'; '1st C.W. - Second, 40th CBW Lead, 41st CBW Third'; Air Commander Lt Col Milton; '3rd ATF same target 30 minutes behind us'; fighter cover plan; 'Descend after target to 21,000''. Results: 18 assigned, 8 abortive, 10 attacked, 1 missing (42-6096). IP Wurzburg; IP turn 1438; bombs away 1441; 23,550 ft true; CIAS 150 mph, TAS 222 mph; true heading 64, track 61, axis of attack 58 true; straight run 60 s (flight record) / 40 s (flak report); 5-degree S-turns on run-in; rally right turn to 130. Route: in at West Schouwen, Turnhout, Duren, right turn at Bad Nauheim, S-turn from Lohr, Karlstadt, ... out at Bourg d'Ault. English coast out Orfordness 1233 at 21,000 ft; enemy coast out Ault 1643 at 21,000 ft; English coast in Beachy Head 1703 at 10,000 ft. Group was 13 min late at target. S-2: escort left / attacks began 1330. Note: the statistical report header mistakenly says 'Mission of 17 August' and '101st Combat Wing' (1st CBW's former provisional number).

title: The Army Air Forces in World War II, Vol. II, Ch. 20 'Pointblank' (Schweinfurt 14 Oct 1943 narrative, pp. 699-704)
author: W. F. Craven and J. L. Cate (eds.), USAF Historical Division (HyperWar transcription)
notes: Official history. 291 B-17s dispatched in two forces, 149 1st BD + 142 3d BD, 'to cross enemy defenses abreast, some 30 miles apart'; one P-47 group per force for penetration, one for withdrawal from 60 mi inland; P-38 group not operational until next day; 2 sqns Spitfire IX sweep; B-24s failed to assemble, 29 flew feint toward Emden; weather prevented withdrawal escort; P-47s turned back near Aachen (~240 mi from British coast); 40th CW 'which led the 1st Division' had lost 7 of its 49 before the target and 29 in total; 28 lost before target overall; sudden course change near IP; 228 bombed; 60 lost, 17 major damage, 121 repairable; German records 38 fighters destroyed, 20 damaged in combat. Rocket tactics described.

title: The Army Air Forces in World War II, Vol. II, Ch. 10 'Over Germany' and diagram 'Bomber Combat Formations, Summer 1943' (p. 332)
author: W. F. Craven and J. L. Cate (eds.), USAF Historical Division (HyperWar transcription)
notes: Text (https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/AAF/II/AAF-II-10.html): combat wing = three combat boxes of 18-21 planes; 54-plane wing flown from April 1943. Diagram: combat box side view lead sqn 25,000 ft, 2d (high) sqn 25,100 ft, 3d (low) sqn 24,750 ft, total box depth 750 ft; plan view lead sqn ahead, high and low sqns behind on either side; combat wing: lead box 25,000, 2d box 24,000, 3d box 26,000, overall 3,000 ft. Summer 1943 doctrine, not mission-specific.

title: Map: Mission to Schweinfurt, 14 October 1943, up to 1440 hours (Craven & Cate Vol. II p. 700)
author: W. F. Craven and J. L. Cate (eds.), USAF Historical Division
notes: Shows 1st and 3d Division tracks on parallel courses across the North Sea and Low Countries, the 3d Division track south of the 1st, a 3d Division dog-leg south then east before converging on Schweinfurt, fighter escort tracks ending near the German border, 2d Division track (diversion) toward the north.

title: The Forts Come Home (1963 retrospective)
author: Air Force Magazine / Air & Space Forces Magazine
notes: 1st AD 149 from nine groups, 48 failed to bomb, 101 attacked, 45 destroyed + 5 crashed/crash-landed/abandoned over England; 3d AD 142 from seven groups, 14 failed to attack, 128 attacked, 15 lost. 305th: 16 took off, 1 aborted, 12 fell before target, 1 after, 2 returned. 306th: 15 went, 5 returned, 10 lost. 384th: only lead ship returned to its field; six down.

title: Death on the High Road: The Schweinfurt Raid
author: HistoryNet (World War II magazine)
notes: 305th could not find the 40th CW and joined the 1st CW; 40th (92nd and 306th only) 'tagged along with the 41st'. Losses: 305th 13 of 15, 306th 12 (conflicts with 10 elsewhere), 92nd/379th/384th 6 each; 3rd BD 15, three groups incl. 100th lost none. Escort: 353rd and 56th FG rendezvoused, 4th FG failed to find bombers, 352nd covered B-24 feint; 55th FG (P-38) not ready. B-24s: 60 scheduled, 29 took off, 21 flew diversion. Internal inconsistencies (351 vs 291 B-17s) noted.

title: Schweinfurt - 14 Oct 43 'Black Thursday' (Robert Hughes account)
author: Robert L. Hughes / 100th Bomb Group Foundation
notes: Participant account. 100th had only 8 crews; two four-ship flights, one (Roane) with the 390th, one (Hughes) with the 95th. Rendezvous with 95th at 2,000 ft 1027; 95th four short in high squadron so 100th flight filled it ('square group'); 1218 rendezvous with 390th formed 13th Combat Wing; English coast out 1218; IP 1447; bombs away 1454; English coast in 1725.

title: Second Schweinfurt raid
author: Wikipedia
notes: Used only as a lead. Group list for both divisions; bombing times 1439-1445 (first force) and 1451-1457 (second); 229 of 291 attacked; loss figures internally inconsistent (60 vs 77).

title: The 306th Bombardment Group (museum page)
author: 306th Bombardment Group Museum, Thurleigh
notes: 18 Fortresses left; 3 returned early with technical problems; 5 completed the mission and returned badly damaged; about 100 crewmen lost.

title: B-17 losses on Schweinfurt mission 14-10-1943 (aircraft database)
author: b17flyingfortress.de
notes: 69 aircraft entries (lost, crashed, battle-damaged) with squadron and MACR numbers. MACR clusters by group: 92nd 844-849 (6), 306th 814-823 (10), 384th 837-842 (6), 379th 954-958 + 1353 (6), 305th 911-922 + 1034 + 779 (13) plus one ambiguous entry (42-29870, MACR 1038), 381st 1037, 351st 1036, 303rd 907, 91st 899, 94th 788/789-792 (5) + Brennan's Circus ditched, 96th 831-836 (6), 95th 855, 390th 858. Unit tags list all historical assignments, so group attribution used the squadron and MACR cluster.

title: 'Black Thursday' October 14, 1943: The Second Schweinfurt Bombing Raid
author: The National WWII Museum
notes: 1st Division led, 3rd trailed; P-47s turned back near Aachen; Ju 88 21 cm rockets from ~1,000 yd; 40th (wing) lost 7 of 49 before target; 60 lost, 17 not airworthy, 121 damaged; German records 31 fighters destroyed, 12 written off, 34 damaged (differs from Craven & Cate).

title: Black Thursday: The second Schweinfurt raid and the legacy beyond
author: DVIDS (citing Martin Caidin, Black Thursday)
notes: 306th: 15 went on to raid, 5 returned, 10 lost; 100 men (35 killed, 65 captured).

title: Black Thursday: The Second Schweinfurt Raid
author: IWM American Air Museum in Britain
notes: 305th: 13 aircraft failed to return, 130 men; Spitfires and P-47s escorted about halfway; Ju 88 rockets from outside defensive range.

title: Schweinfurt - The Battle Within the Battle for the U.S. 8th Air Force
author: Capt. David Reichert, Air & Space Power Chronicles (Air University)
notes: NOT READ IN FULL (server returned 403). Only search-engine excerpts seen: the 1st CW was missing its low group; the 305th filled that slot after radio contact with the wing commander; the assigned low group, the 381st, later joined up on the wing's high group, the 351st. Treat as PROBABLE until read.

title: The Schweinfurt Raid - America's Worst Day
author: WarHistory.org
notes: Low reliability (typos such as '350th Group' for 305th; claims 96th lost 14 on return, contradicted by MACR data). Useful leads: 3rd Division left English coast ~10 mi south of Harwich at 1225, five minutes after the 1st; picked up 53 P-47s at Belgian coast, lost them after Eupen; sharp turn south at Eupen toward Trier/Mosel, then east to IP near Darmstadt at 1405 (time doubtful); 96th led the 3rd Division.

title: B-17 Pilot Training Manual, formation section (as reproduced by The Vintage News)
author: Headquarters AAF, Office of Flying Safety / The Vintage News
notes: Training doctrine (stateside), not 8th AF combat SOP: minimum 50 ft wingtip clearance and 50 ft nose-to-tail in the Vee; at least 50 ft vertical between elements; high squadron 150 ft above and 100 ft behind lead squadron, low squadron 150 ft below and 100 ft behind. Manual publication date not shown on the page.

title: Combat box
author: Wikipedia (citing Roger A. Freeman, The Mighty Eighth War Manual, 1991, pp. 42-43; Martin Bowman, USAAF Handbook, 1997, pp. 46-48)
notes: 21-plane group box standard from 13 Jan 1943 through Sept 1943 (Bowman); 54-plane wing box typically ~3,000 ft vertical, 7,000 ft deep, 2,000 ft across (Freeman); 36-plane group box introduced October 1943 (Freeman) - not used on 14 Oct per S1/S2 group sizes; early squadrons ~150 ft between highest and lowest aircraft.

title: Flying in formation
author: b17flyingfortress.de
notes: 54-aircraft wing (Feb 1943 wedge) 1.3 miles wide and 0.3 miles front-to-back; 'Javelin' groups at 1.5-mile intervals; end-1943 groups at 4-mile intervals. Unsourced.

title: 398th Bomb Group Combat Formations
author: Wally Blackwell, 398th BG Memorial Association (2003)
notes: 1944-45 context. Element wingmen 'one wing length horizontally from and one wing length behind the Element lead'; squadron distances in hundreds of feet, group in thousands.
